demonstrations.review: This was the relaunch of the Wonder Woman comic series. There were hints of a good story but they weren't allowed to develop. Since I haven't followed the series I have no idea if any depth has ever been added. The use of comic book titles to introduce two characters was lame. NEMESIS is probably known to many readers but I doubt there are many younger fans who even know about the Wally Wood / Walt Simonson HERCULES series that ran what? Twelve issues, if I remember correctly. This book reminds me of a joke we used to tell about Image Comics: Image Comics is the right name. Substance Comics would be a lie. demonstrations.item_text:

Created by legendary comics creator Jack Kirby, The New Gods are a group of immortal "gods" from the "Fourth World", which consists of the two warring planets New Genesis and Apokolips. demonstrations.review:
WARNING!!! Contains plot spoilers. This is a companion to the Countdown to Final Crisis (although the cover doesn't indicate that). It is also an excellent story. The New Gods are being murdered - their souls are being ripped out of their bodies. The story begins with the third murder; the first two occur in The Countdown to Final Crisis and the end of this book (kinda-sorta) sends you back to that series. For that reason it is imperfect. The fact that I give imperfection 5 stars tells you what a good job Jim Starlin did in telling and penciling this story. An enhanced* Mr. Miracle and Superman take the investigation from earth to New Genesis and the rest of the story proceeds from there.
*Another imperfection - anyone who isn't hardwired into the DC Universe (like me) might want to go back and read the story that brought that enhancement about. It isn't mentioned. I used the asterisk behind "enhanced" in homage to the way such references used to be made.
But, in any case, this is well worth reading...even though the story is not complete. But, given The Final Crisis, that is, unfortunately, to be expected.

demonstrations.item_text:
Rise of the Superheroes: Greatest Silver Age Comic Books and Characters
Hardcover – Download: Adobe Reader, May 8, 2018

They Could Be Heroes Rise of the Superheroes--Greatest Silver Age Comic Books and Characters is a visual and entertaining adventure exploring one of the most popular and significant eras of comic book history. From 1956 to 1970, the era gave us Spider-Man, The Avengers, X-Men, The Incredible Hulk, Iron Man and a flurry of other unforgettable and formidable characters. The Silver Age redefined and immortalized superheroes as the massive pop culture titans they are today. Lavishly illustrated with comic book covers and original art, the book chronicles:   • The new frontier of DC Comics, with a revamped Batman, Superman and Wonder Woman, and new characters including Hawkman   • Marvel's new comics featuring Thor and The Fantastic Four   • The pop art years that saw Batman's "new look" and the TV series   • Independent characters, including Fat Fury and T.H.U.N.D.E.R. Agents   • Spotlights new and re-imagined superheroes, like Wonder Woman, who have become central to modern pop culture   • Includes values of these comics, which are popular with collectorsThanks to the Silver Age, superheroes are bigger and badder than ever.
demonstrations.review: I received this book as a gift from my wife. The author and I are the same age, so it was fun to literally relive that period from his perspective. It was also a source of chagrin (with a ruefull grin) to see the current value of books that I remember at least reading, to say nothing of owning at one time or another. I do wish it had just a bit more. The author is a fan of Neal Adams, and rightfully so. Kudos to Dick Giordano and Tatjana Wood for their contributions to Neal's work, at DC, and to Tom Palmer's contributions to his work at Marvel. But there was another driving force at the same time, at Marvel, that also pushed comic art in the adventuresome direction that it is still going, today: Jim Steranko, especially his run on "Nick Fury and His Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D." , both in "Strange Tales" and in the Nick Fury titled series. The S.H.I.E.L.D. TV series is not even mentioned in the book, compounding this apparent oversight. To be fair, Steranko's artwork is shown, but his impact is, on the whole, overlooked. Fun fact: Jack Kirby's "Fourth World" series at DC is mentioned, along with covers of each of the 4 books that comprised the series. One of these, "Mr. Miracle", had its character inspired by an escape artist that Kirby actually knew: Jim Steranko. I recommend this book, but, with just a little more, I could have recommended it a lot more.

Wendy, Darling

A lush, feminist re-imagining on what happened to Wendy after Neverland, for fans of Circe and The Mere Wife. LOCUS AWARD FINALIST FOR BEST FIRST NOVEL Find the second star from the right, and fly straight on ’til morning, all the way to Neverland, a children’s paradise with no rules, no adults, only endless adventure and enchanted forests – all led by the charismatic boy who will never grow old.  But Wendy Darling grew up. She has a husband and a young daughter called Jane, a life in London. But one night, after all these years, Peter Pan returns. Wendy finds him outside her daughter’s window, looking to claim a new mother for his Lost Boys. But instead of Wendy, he takes Jane.  Now a grown woman, a mother, a patient and a survivor, Wendy must follow Peter back to Neverland to rescue her daughter and finally face the darkness at the heart of the island…
demonstrations.review:
I hadn’t heard of A. C. Wise before a few months ago, when I read her story, “The Amazing Exploding Women of the Early Twentieth Century” in issue 122 of Apex Magazine. I loved it and started following her on Twitter, where I found out she would soon be releasing her first novel. I preordered it on a whim and I’m so glad I did.

Wendy, Darling brings us back into the life of Wendy, from J. M. Barrie’s Peter Pan, just has Peter has returned many years later to steal away her daughter, Jane. From there, the novel follows three lines: Wendy searching for her daughter in 1931; Jane, trapped in a darker Neverland with an ominous Peter Pan; and Wendy in 1917-1920, trapped in an institution by John and Michael, after refusing to give up her belief in the flying boy and his magic island.

The novel is well-paced and immediately gripping, but the thing I applaud the most is how Wise has made Barrie’s characters her own. She managed it beautifully, making Wendy, Peter, and the rest familiar, yet darkly different. Peter is both the boy we remember, and something shadowy and sharp-toothed, with danger lurking just behind his glinting eyes. And anyone who wanted to believe in fairytales as a child (or adult), whose imagination has ever run wholly wild, will empathize with this Wendy, unable to let Neverland go, even at the cost of hospitalization and a strained relationship with her brothers. The soft Wendy we knew becomes fierce and motherly, but in a real and raw way, not the playful pretend of her childhood. There a few other familiar characters prancing through the pages of Wendy, Darling (and some new ones to fall in love with), but I’ll leave you to discover them, yourself.

Not only is this new Neverland cast in sinister shadow and dark magic in a way that draws the reader in and brings them into its mythology and magic, but Wise also skillfully brings the reader into the adult lives and relationships back in London in a way that is heartfelt, deep and true. I’m not much of a crier, but a few of the scenes between Wendy and Michael brought me to the edge of tears.
If you’re hoping for a wonderful fantasy in A. C. Wise’s Wendy, Darling you’ll get it. You’ll also get a touch of horror and a bit of romance. It’s a story of siblings, a mother-daughter tale, and also a retelling of the dark side of fairy tales, of the terrible things that can happen when we let childhood go…or the things that happen when we don’t. This book has something for everyone who ever believed in magic, in monsters in the closet, or anyone who has longed for love and childhood lost.

This is great for a beginner like myself.  I love that she writes the patterns so they are useable for any method of knitting.  I am a cuff-down magic looper, and it's great to know I can take any of her techniques and use them on magic loop.  She also makes simple mathematical equations so you can take you foot measurements, a calculator and get a custom fit.  It's a really simple, easy to read book with tons of accessible information.  This is one of the best knitting books I have ever picked up.

demonstrations.item_text:
I Had Trouble in Getting to Solla Sollew
Hardcover – August 12, 1965

A perennial favorite and a perfect gift for anyone starting a new phase in their life! Dr. Seuss tackles the struggles of everyday life’s—difficult people, bullies, bad weather, political unrest, even crowds—in the rhyming picture book I Had Trouble in Getting to Solla Sollew. When our hero stubs his toe, he decides to find a less troublesome place to live. Soon he's off on a journey "to the City of Solla Sollew, on the banks of the beautiful River Wah-Hoo, where they never have troubles! At least, very few." But between his encounters with the Midwinter Jicker and the Perilous Poozer of Pompelmoose Pass, he soon finds out that confronting his problems might actually be easier than running away from them. A funny story that can be read purely for entertainment, I Had Trouble in Getting to Solla Sollew is ideal for sparking discussions. It’s message—that the best way to deal with an obstacle is by tackling it head-on—makes this an perfect gift for all ages and occasions—especially graduations!
demonstrations.review: This is a Seuss book that we'd never heard of until we found it at my grandmother in law's house.  We read it to the kids, they loved it, and so did we, so we bought our own copy and it's become a frequently read selection to my 2- and 4-year olds. It's a great selection about how the grass isn't always greener on the other side and to be happy with what you've got (or where you live).

demonstrations.item_text:
Dear Zoo: A Lift-the-Flap Book
Board book – Lift the flap, May 8, 2007

Rod Campbell’s classic lift-the-flap book Dear Zoo has been a firm favorite with toddlers and parents alike ever since it was first published in 1982. Young readers love lifting the flaps to discover the animals the zoo has sent—a monkey, a lion, and even an elephant! But will they ever find the perfect pet? With bright, bold artwork, a catchy refrain, and a whole host of favorite animals, Dear Zoo is a must for every child’s bookshelf.
demonstrations.review: I love that the flaps are made of fairly sturdy paper.  My one year old can really do some damage, and while she has managed to bend them a bit, she has not succeeded in tearing. This is one of her favorite books to flip through and open all the flaps!

demonstrations.item_text:
Chicka Chicka Boom Boom (Board Book)
Board book – Illustrated, January 1, 2012

There is always enough room on your child’s bookshelf for this Classic Board Book edition of the rollicking alphabet chant that has been a children’s favorite for over thirty years! A told B, and B told C, “I’ll meet you at the top of the coconut tree” In this lively alphabet rhyme, all the letters of the alphabet race each other up the coconut tree. Will there be enough room? Oh, no—Chicka Chicka Boom! Boom! Countless children—and their parents—can joyfully recite the familiar words of this beloved alphabet chant. Bill Martin, Jr., and John Archambault’s rhythmic text keeps the beat with Caldecott Honor illustrator Lois Ehlert’s bold, cheerful art. This winning combination has made the Chicka Chicka series an enduring classic.
demonstrations.review: This is a great alphabet book.  It is super fun to read to my baby and toddler, so much so that my little girl often tries to take it and read it instead of me.  I get bored reading the same books over and over, but Chicka Chicka Boom Boom has an almost musical beat to it that makes it enjoyable for me, as well as my kids.

target.item_text:
The Millionaire Next Door: The Surprising Secrets of America's Wealthy
Paperback – November 16, 2010

The bestselling The Millionaire Next Door identifies seven common traits that show up again and again among those who have accumulated wealth. Most of the truly wealthy in this country don't live in Beverly Hills or on Park Avenue-they live next door. This new edition, the first since 1998, includes a new foreword for the twenty-first century by Dr. Thomas J. Stanley.
target.review: This book was a really good read, but I was left with a few unanswered questions.  In this book, you will learn about the PAWS (prodigious accumulators of wealth) and the UAWS (Under Accumulators of Wealth). You will also learn about EOC (Economic Outpatient Care - or basically supporting your adult children financially).  I must admit that that many parts of the book encouraged me (I felt that I was mostly on the right track of being a PAW), but parts of the book left me feeling a little helpless (i.e. I work hard and take risks so that my kids will never have to experience hardship and poverty like I once did, and I may have unwittingly turned them into adults that will need EOC).  I choose to have a nice house in a good neighborhood, because I want my family to be safe, have access to good public schools, and friends who are not into drugs or gangs (not that it can't happen anywhere, but I'm trying to minimize exposure).  I buy used imported luxury cars because nowadays they actually have a lower Total Cost of Ownership (see Edmunds dot com), they are demonstrably more reliable (see JD Powers) and they typically score much higher safety ratings than any basic domestic cars. Not to mention that my experience with the dealerships have been night and day.  Lastly, what is the point to all of the wealth accumulation if you cannot enjoy it and share it with the ones you love?  If I were single and had no children, I'm certain that I would be worth $10 Million dollars by now (could have taken more career risks and been more mobile, with fewer expenses), but I'm much happier, and wish I could have afforded to have more children.  I'll have to be content with grandkids someday.  I'll read "The Millionaire Mind" next to see if I get any answers.

demonstrations.item_text:
Mastering Pizza: The Art and Practice of Handmade Pizza, Focaccia, and Calzone [A Cookbook]
Hardcover – August 28, 2018

A revolutionary guide to making delicious pizza at home, offering a variety of base doughs so that your pizza will turn out perfect no matter what kind of oven or equipment you have. Pizza remains America's favorite food, but one that many people hesitate to make at home. In Mastering Pizza , award-winning chef Marc Vetri tackles the topic with his trademark precision, making perfect pizza available to anyone. The recipes—gleaned from years spent researching recipes in Italy and perfecting them in America—have a variety of base doughs of different hydration levels, which allow home cooks to achieve the same results with a regular kitchen oven as they would with a professional pizza oven. The book covers popular standards like Margherita and Carbonara while also featuring unexpected toppings such as mussels and truffles—and even a dessert pizza made with Nutella. With transporting imagery from Italy and hardworking step-by-step photos to demystify the process, Mastering Pizza will help you make pizza as delicious as you find in Italy.
demonstrations.review:
I borrowed this book from the library. Yesterday I started to prep for making pizza this weekend. I tried the Old School Naples Dough at 70% hydration. The method and amount for starting the yeast seemed a little strange to me based on my experience with Ken Forkish's book. You add 0.1g. (1/32 tsp) of active dry yeast to salty cold water (two things yeast don't like). I added all the other ingredients in the exact amounts weighed in grams on a scale. I even used King Arthur Bread flour (which I like - but ususally use Antimo Caputo 00 for Napalitano style pizza). The result? After a warm (72F) ferment for 6 hours, no discernable activity. I decided to let this cold rest and after 24 hours, there is barely any activity (faint alcohol fermentation smell, and no perceptible rise). This small amount of yeast and adding it to cold (55F) salted water is not a typo on this recipe. His other recipes use the same tiny amounts of yeast and salt added to cold water. My yeast was fresh instant dry yeast, and I have plenty of experience making pizza's of all styles. I just don't see the point in wasting a day prepping a pizza dough when it seems to be such a crap shoot despite following the directions to a T. I was hoping to find the ancient secrets of Naples in this book, but it looks like I was sold a fugazi (or at least borrow one from the library). I do like some of his discussion on hydration and cold fermentation, and the book is very attractive. Unfortunately the method of proofing the dough seems unique (odd, and counterintuitive), and left me with a large bowl of paste instead of anything resembling pizza dough.
**UPDATE** I continued to let this dough warm ferment (72F) for an additional day. Once it showed signs of life, I balled it up and let it continue to cold ferment another day. So I started out on a Wednesday morning and by Friday evening I had pizza dough that seemed useable. I made 3 pizzas with it, and my family loved the crust. I think that using a high hydration dough is a really good technique for cooking pizza at home in a 550F oven. High Hydration dough is a huge pain to work with vs 60% hydration. I may try this recipe again, but proof the yeast first in warmer water with no salt. Then depending on its activity I will cold ferment it for three days. The recipe as written states that your dough will be ready in about 6 hours. There was absolutely no sign of yeast activity in my dough after 6 hours at room temp. In the end, the pizza turned out good. I was happy to achieve these result using King Arthur vs the much more expensive and hard to find Antimo Caputo 00. I attribute my success to using a 70% hydration recipe in a 550F degree oven. That is a bit of wisdom that I learned from this book, so I will give credit where it is due.

demonstrations.item_text:
How to Keep Your Volkswagen Alive: A Manual of Step-by-Step Procedures for the Compleat Idiot
Paperback – August 29, 2001

First published in 1969, this classic manual of automotive repair equips VW owners with the practical skills to keep their Volkswagen running smoothly. Inside you'll find: Expert knowledge on any air-cooled Volkswagen built through 1978, including Bugs, Karmann Ghias, vans, and campers Expert knowledge on any air-cooled Volkswagen built through 1978, including Bugs, Karmann Ghias, vans, and campers Easy-to-understand, fun-to-read information for novice and veteran mechanics alike, with anecdotal descriptions and clear language to help take the mystery out of diagnostic, maintenance, and repair procedures Easy-to-understand, fun-to-read information for novice and veteran mechanics alike, with anecdotal descriptions and clear language to help take the mystery out of diagnostic, maintenance, and repair procedures Trusted advice from the late John Muir, whose in-depth knowledge and sense of humor have guided Volkswagen enthusiasts for nearly 50 years Trusted advice from the late John Muir, whose in-depth knowledge and sense of humor have guided Volkswagen enthusiasts for nearly 50 years Hand-lettered with intricate hand-drawn illustrations throughout Hand-lettered with intricate hand-drawn illustrations throughout Updated information on problem-solving, with new photos and an updated resource list Updated information on problem-solving, with new photos and an updated resource list Packed with trusted insight, troubleshooting tips, and clear directions, How to Keep Your Volkswagen Alive is the ultimate VW manual.
demonstrations.review: This book came with my 1967 Super Beetle.  It may be hard to imagine, but in addition to being an extremely useful book for maintaining your Volkswagen, it was also an enjoyable read, with fabulous graphics.  I owned that wonderful beetle for 6 years, and this book (and that car) turned me into a mechanic.  I accidentally sold the car one day.  I was having a garage sale, and my sweet beetle was sitting in the garage when a lady asked me "how much for the beetle"?  I jokingly said $2000 because I had no intention of selling it (I paid $600 for it).  A few days later I was out working in the front yard when a car drove past and then backed up.  The same woman rolled down the window and asked "Are you the guy selling the Beetle"?  I responded "I guess so."  She had her 19 year old  son with her, and I took him for a test drive, and she handed me $2000 cash. I asked the kid, "Do you know how to work on cars"?  He responded "No."  I handed him my worn, spiral bound copy of How to Keep Your Volkswagen Alive, and said "You will."  They drove off in the car, and I felt like someone had just taken my favorite dog.  Even though the car is long gone, I am thinking about buying a new copy of this book, just to help keep the memories alive.  That car required constant maintenance, but it provided me with reliable transportation and a priceless education.

demonstrations.item_text:
Basic Economics
Hardcover – December 2, 2014

The bestselling citizen's guide to economics Basic Economics is a citizen's guide to economics, written for those who want to understand how the economy works but have no interest in jargon or equations. Bestselling economist Thomas Sowell explains the general principles underlying different economic systems: capitalist, socialist, feudal, and so on. In readable language, he shows how to critique economic policies in terms of the incentives they create, rather than the goals they proclaim. With clear explanations of the entire field, from rent control and the rise and fall of businesses to the international balance of payments, this is the first book for anyone who wishes to understand how the economy functions. This fifth edition includes a new chapter explaining the reasons for large differences of wealth and income between nations.  Drawing on lively examples from around the world and from centuries of history, Sowell explains basic economic principles for the general public in plain English.
demonstrations.review: I love books on economics, and this book is my new favorite.  You will not find a single chart in this book, and it is written nearly like "Explain it like I'm 5 years old."  Of course a subject this complex (it is called the Dismal Science after all) cannot exactly be dumbed down to the level that a five year old could understand, Dr. Sowell does an amazing job explaining market dynamics like: Price, Utility, Scarcity, Productivity, Protectionism, etc. in ways that should make it clear to anyone who is literate. The language that he uses is meant to convey the idea, not to impress you with his intellect and vocabulary (which is amazing).  Dr. Sowell's newly added Chapter 23 on "International Disparities in Wealth" should be required reading for Socialists and Marxists.  Here's the strategy that I used to get through the 704 pages of this book.  Read one chapter start to finish at a time.  Each chapter, is for the most part, a self contained lesson. Later in the book, there are references to earlier sections, but they are annotated so that you can go back and reference them.  I was curious to read Chapter 23, and skipped ahead to that one. I was able to follow it without having read all of the previous chapters.  I later re-read it in sequence.  When my wife saw me reading this huge book and asked me about it, I simply put on a youtube video of Thomas Sowell: Common Sense in a Senseless World.  This book is filled with great real world examples of what happens when politicians try to manipulate the market (economy) with laws that inevitably favor one group over another. It also explains how politicians take the short view (their goal being getting re-elected) versus appreciating the impact their laws have on every American, or the world as a whole.  Today's buzzword seems to be "Equity" where equal opportunity is not enough, but we must strive for an equal outcome.  A read of this book will make you realize that the only way for us to achieve an equal outcome is for our society to allocate resources in a less productive manner.  This will inevitably bring the outcome for the vast majority down.  In America today, even the impoverished have lives that are more secure than those in the third world (including the socialist utopias of Venezuela and Cuba).  For those that think Dr. Sowell might be out of touch with those who are impoverished, you should read his bio, and realize that he started life under extremely difficult circumstances (orphaned, impoverished, drafted into the military).  He was in fact, at one time in his 20's, a Marxist.  Thankfully, he experienced an awakening to how things really work and was able to share that with us in this amazing book.

demonstrations.item_text:
Fahrenheit 451
Paperback – January 10, 2012

Nearly seventy years after its original publication, Ray Bradbury’s internationally acclaimed novel Fahrenheit 451 stands as a classic of world literature set in a bleak, dystopian future. Today its message has grown more relevant than ever before. Guy Montag is a fireman. His job is to destroy the most illegal of commodities, the printed book, along with the houses in which they are hidden. Montag never questions the destruction and ruin his actions produce, returning each day to his bland life and wife, Mildred, who spends all day with her television “family.” But when he meets an eccentric young neighbor, Clarisse, who introduces him to a past where people didn’t live in fear and to a present where one sees the world through the ideas in books instead of the mindless chatter of television, Montag begins to question everything he has ever known.
demonstrations.review: We ran out of firewood, so I used this book to keep our house warm for the night.  JK, I read this book in 9th grade, and recently my DD was assigned this as required reading in school.  She actually commented on how much she liked the book last night at dinner, after bragging about how she just aced her test on it.

demonstrations.item_text: $20 Per Gallon: How the Rise in the Price of Gas Will Change Our Lives for the Better
demonstrations.review:
UPDATE: April 2020 COVID-19 Gas is nearly $1.00 a gallon (I filled up my SUV yesterday for $17.00 - less than a RT ticket on the Metra from Evanston to Union Station). Oil is trading at less tham $12 A BARREL (about 27 cents a gallon). WTI Crude futures are trading in negative territory! Mr. Steiner is batting .000 Why do I come back here every few years to gloat about the author's failure to predict the price of gasoline? For one, his book was alarmist (just like most of the Global Warming, er...Climate Change, er..now CLIMATE CRISIS! people). We're currently in the midst of a pandemic, and the price of a gallon of gas has dropped below $1.00 a gallon in Wisconsin. Secondly, I felt like the author was rooting for gas to rise to $20 a gallon. He felt that we would all be so much more enlightened if we all lived like Europeans in crowded cities and rode public transportation. HOW'S THAT WORKING OUT FOR YA? For those of you who think that world will be a better place and we will "save the planet" if we live packed together more densely and relying on the government to control our ability to move around, just remember back to the time when you we're stuck at home during the Coronavirus, and people all around you were losing their jobs. That's what gas at $20 a gallon would really look like. When we finally start to recover from this Coronavirus situation, the saving grace (at least for Americans) Is that we will not be hit by the double whammy of high gas prices. Hopefully this will help re-start our economy more quickly. Best of luck to all of you!

UPDATE: December 2015..Gas is well below $2.00 a gallon ($1.62 locally). Oil is trading below $35 a barrel and predicted to go as low as $20 a barrel. When people say "Peak Oil," others laugh. I, for one, am glad that the price of gasoline is back down. It is a real economic relief to nearly everyone. Too bad Mr. Steiner isn't able to take advantage of the savings as the price of a train ticket on the Metra, and the CTA Purple line have gone up dramatically in the last year. Ohh, gas will hit $20 a gallon one day. Probably when this country is embroiled in it's next civil war. Merry Christmas!

UPDATE: December 2014.. Gas is down below $2.50 and Brent Crude traded yesterday at $53.00 a barrel. Could this book have been more off the mark? Milk will hit $20 a gallon around the same time gasoline does because of inflation.

In all honesty this book nearly deserves a 2 star rating, for some of the creative fear the author conjurs up. But, if you are like me, you only read the 1 stars and 5 stars. I read this book awhile ago (2009) when gas prices had spiked. A friend of mine loaned it to me, and I was intrigued by him asking "how can one profit from this"?

Fast forward 3 years and gas prices are below $3.00 a gallon in some parts of the USA. An earthquake and tsunami once again opened the world's eyes to the dangers of nuclear power (let alone we have all but forgotten about the problem of nuclear waste). Solyndra and GE have shown the people what folly the "Green Economy" is.

All of his lousy predictions aside, what really turned me off to this book was the holier than thou theme in his writing style. Even the title makes it clear that he relishes the idea of all of us being forced to move to cities and ride public transportation, and eat seasonally available organic produce by florescent light just like all those "enlightened" Europeans do. I lived in Europe for many years, and all I can say is "Thanks, but, no thanks." People don't live like that because they are enlightened, they live like that because of economics. To think that we will all somehow be happier being forced (through Gov't taxation or corporate greed) to live a less comfortable life, is like praising self flagellation. The truth is that the Chicken Little's have been crying that the sky is falling for over 40 years now. Technology, not taxation will solve our imagined energy crisis. Mark my words, when that happens, some other crisis will be conjured up so that some government somewhere can institute a tax on it, or some mega corporation can profit from it (To wit..Ozone Hole - Gov't institutes a massive tax on CFC's and DuPont is standing by with a new replacement that costs 4x as much as the CFC's (which are inert and never wear out- so people could just keep recycling) and both the Gov't and DuPont make a killing. Have you been to Home Depot lately and checked the price on those new LED light bulbs??? I cannot believe that GE has the nerve to put their name on the package. Couple that with the fact that they are the largest wind turbine maker around, and you can see that they are making money coming and going, while the gov't keeps proposing tax increases on energy and CO2). The winners are corporation and gov't. The losers are the citizenry that allows this corruption to continue unchecked.

Imagine, telling people 30 years ago that the government would someday propose a tax on a colorless, odorless, gas that is essential to plant life (and beer carbonation)......

All in all, this book is just depressing, and lacks any persuasive argument for why our lives will be better living in a crowded city riding public transportation. My feeling is that this is the lifestyle he has chosen for himself, and he is looking for affirmation. UPDATE: Mr. Steiner just wrote a piece for Forbes titled: The Top 5 Ski Resorts in the United States. He sings the praises of Jackson Hole, Alta/Snowbird, Telluride, Squaw Valley and Vail/Beaver Creek. As luck would have it, I have been to all of those places. Interestingly, I had to take a private jet and a car to get there. While there, I observed a bunch of wealthy people indulging in recreation on the slopes of mountains that were cleared of (CO2 reducing)trees. They were riding electrically powered gondolas, and quaffing beer and wine that was brought in by diesel powered trucks, while a tree was being burned in a firepit. They then hop into their Land Rovers and drive back to their vacation homes that they occupy less than 4 week a year. Yeah I can't wait for $20.00 a gallon gas too.

Undoubtedly gas will one day reach $20 a gallon, but it will be because our government's irrational monetary policy will make hyper-inflation the only practical way for us to repay our debt to China. I tried to bet my friend who loaned me the book that gasoline would be back under $3.00 a gallon before it ever reached $20. He wisely decided against taking the bet.

target.item_text:
Fear Has a Name: A Pulse-Pounding Contemporary Christian Thriller (The Crittendon Files Book 1)
Kindle Edition

A Haunting Name From the Past . . . Granger Meade was mentally scarred as a boy by his religious zealot parents. He was bullied at school for his quiet, oafish appearance, which naturally made him a loner and outcast.But one girl treated him differently—Pamela Wagner. Pam talked to Granger, took an interest, listened, made him feel like a human being. She cared when no one else did, and Granger loved her for it; and still does 20 years later.So Granger goes back to their Ohio town. Back to Pamela. But she is happily married to reporter Jack Crittendon, who's embroiled in a time-sensitive story about a pastor who's disappeared and left a suicide note; a case swirling with suspicion and talk of scandal. With tension on every page, Amazon #1 Best-Selling author Creston Mapes demonstrates why he is a "Top Pick" among mystery, fiction and thriller lovers. Fans of DiAnn Mills, Terri Blackstock, Susan Sleeman, Alton Gansky, Karen Kingsbury, and Robin Patchen will love this thriller from award-winning and bestselling author Creston Mapes. Reader praise for Fear Has a Name ★★★★★ Gripping Suspense, Edge of Your Seat Reading. Fear Has a Name is a gripping Christian suspense novel that gives you everything you want from cover to cover. You will be on the edge of your seat wondering what is going to happen next. The best thing about this novel from a Christian readers perspective is the way that faith, mercy and forgiveness are woven seamlessly throughout the book . . . A very good read for anyone who likes Christian Suspense and drama. Once you start reading you won't be able to stop until it's done.★★★★★ First time I have read a Christian suspense novel . . . I'm hooked. Honestly not sure how I stumbled on to this book but have found a new genre. I have read a lot of suspense and crime novels and didn't know there were Christian suspense novels until this one! Creston Mapes is an incredible author. Powerful storytelling with believable characters and plenty of suspense.★★★★★ Fast-Paced Christian Thriller. Two intriguing storylines converge in the end . . . I read late into the night, and after I went to sleep, I had a nightmare about being kidnapped like Pamela. I woke up and had to finish the book before I went back to sleep.★★★★★ This is an excellent and gripping Christian Fiction thriller that will keep you glued to the pages until the very end. Or, if you are like me, it will keep you up all night because you can’t walk away from it. The story line is enticing and action packed.★★★★★ Highly Recommend. This was a great read! I enjoy clean suspense. The plot was well laid out. The Christian themes were strong. This book is a ministry, and it was nice to see such a strong statement of faith presented in a story that was full of real life hurt, pain, and imperfection.★★★★★ Creston Mapes has a new series called "The Crittendon Files" that promises to be his best writing yet . . . We aren't supposed to make a personal connection and actually feel empathy with the bad guy in a book, right? But Granger is, in my opinion, one of the best written antagonists I have ever read. And the final paragraph in this book really hit home for me. I mean...it was a jaw dropping wow moment that I haven't had since Ted Dekker's "Heaven" series . . . If you only buy one book this year, make sure you buy this one . . . It's that good.
target.review: I loved this book, and will read ore of Mr.Male's books. It is so rare to find an author who can satisfy my love of mystery/thrillers without curse words or sexual situations and innuendo!  This book kept me on the edge of my seat!

demonstrations.item_text:
Shadows Among Us (Doctors of Darkness Book 4)
Kindle Edition

Evil is closer than you think. Psychologist, Mollie Roark, had it all. A hotshot husband, a beautiful daughter, a successful career, and a fancy house on the Napa hillside. She’d finally made it. Left her troubled past and her crazy father far behind her.But two years ago, the unspeakable happened. Her daughter’s burned body turned up on the shores of Lake Berryessa just days after her fifteenth birthday. The police seem certain Dakota fell victim to the Shadow Man, the prolific serial killer who had terrorized the Napa Valley for two decades. Mollie’s normal life is now anything but. Childless, divorced, and unemployed, she’s barely staying afloat. She’s got one mission. To find the scumbag who killed her daughter and make him pay. When a mysterious old man shows up at her door seeking absolution and promising answers, it’s impossible to resist. But the deeper she goes inside his mind, the shakier her sanity becomes. Everyone is a suspect. No one is innocent. Because Mollie knows evil may be as close as her own shadow. - Reader Praise for Shadows- "I've been in the mood for creepy reads...I swear I think Ellery Kane can read my mind." "Bottom line, perfection!""Shadows...has got to be the deepest and most jarring of them all. The writing,as always, was perfection. The characters were developed so well, I found myself hurting with them...I couldn't put this book down!" About the Series... Straight from the mind of a forensic psychologist comes an addictive new series of betrayal, lust, revenge, and murder. These doctors earned their degrees from the dark side. And once you start reading, you won't be able to stop.
demonstrations.review: I have read 3 of Kane's books counting this one.  The characters are like people I know - as a teacher you see it all. While I was reading this one, I would catch myself holding my breath.  It was like the deconstruction of a family, not just a mystery. Highly recommend this book. I read it non-stop.

demonstrations.item_text:
The Lost Ones
Kindle Edition

Some secrets are better left undiscovered. When a nine-year-old girl goes missing in Harwood Forest, the search for her brings back memories of an unsolved double murder some forty years earlier. Could the key to Erin Jackson’s disappearance lie in the bloody fate of Elijah and Joanna Ingham, bludgeoned to death while their young daughters slept? Were the Inghams really the victims of opportunistic burglars—or a more sinister fate? The woods are combed for signs of the child, but Erin’s brother, Jake, mounts his own investigation, uncovering evidence that puts the Inghams’ daughters—vanished Rachel and ‘crazy’ Mary—in the frame. Meanwhile, Erin’s father suspects that the ragtag army of eco-warriors besieging his quarry development may have something to hide. As devastating secrets and betrayals are revealed, the Jackson family is brought to a breaking point. But time is running out. Erin is still missing and Jake’s unorthodox enquiries have left him dangerously exposed. They must find Erin and lay the past to rest—before they become its latest victims.
demonstrations.review: I could not put this book down!  The storyline kept me enthralled til the end of the book. Characters were well fleshed out, and the twists and turns keep you turning pages no matter the time.  Thank you for a spellbinding read!

demonstrations.item_text:
Ocean Prey (A Prey Novel Book 31)

Fan-favorite heroes Lucas Davenport and Virgil Flowers join forces on a deadly maritime case in the remarkable new novel from #1 New York Times -bestselling author John Sandford. An off-duty Coast Guardsman is fishing with his family when he calls in some suspicious behavior from a nearby boat. It's a snazzy craft, slick and outfitted with extra horsepower, and is zipping along until it slows to pick up a surfaced diver . . . a diver who was apparently alone, without his own boat, in the middle of the ocean. None of it makes sense unless there's something hinky going on, and his hunch is proved right when all three Guardsmen who come out to investigate are shot and killed.They're federal officers killed on the job, which means the case is the FBI's turf. When the FBI's investigation stalls out, they call in Lucas Davenport. And when his case turns lethal, Davenport will need to bring in every asset he can claim, including a detective with a fundamentally criminal mind: Virgil Flowers.
demonstrations.review: I love all of Stanford's Prey books.  I've read every one.  This one is one of the best!  Lots of action some humor and great characters. If I would change anything, it would be to use less foul language.  These books are all winners! I highly recommend them!

demonstrations.item_text:
Evidence: An Alex Delaware Novel
Kindle Edition

BONUS: This edition contains an excerpt from Jonathan Kellerman's Victims. In a half-built mansion in Los Angeles, a watchman stumbles onto the bodies of a young couple—murdered and left in a gruesome postmortem embrace. Veteran homicide cop Milo Sturgis is shocked at the sight: a twisted crime that only Milo and psychologist Alex Delaware can hope to solve. While the female victim’s identity remains in question, her companion is ID’d as eco-friendly architect Desmond Backer, notorious for his power to seduce women. The deeper Milo and Alex dig for clues, the longer the list of suspects grows. But when the investigation veers suddenly in a startling direction, it’s the investigators who may wind up on the wrong end of a cornered predator’s final fury.
demonstrations.review: I have always loved Keller man's Alex Delaware books. I am reading Evidence on my kindle, and page 247 is completely blank. On 248 I can tell I've missed something. Is there any thing you can do? I couldn't find anywhere to report

target.item_text:
Mulholland Dive: Three Stories
Kindle Edition

Three never-before-collected short stories from #1 New York Times bestselling author Michael ConnellyIn "Cahoots," a backroom poker game turns deadly when a cheater is exposed. In "Mulholland Dive," a man who deciphers the hidden codes of accident scenes investigates a fatality off L.A.'s most fabled roadway. In "Two-Bagger," an obsessed cop tails an ex-con he believes is about to carry out a contract killing.Together these gripping, unforgettable stories show that Michael Connelly "knows the workings of the LAPD and the streets of the City of Angels like he knows his own name" ( Boston Globe ). [Word count: 14,054]
target.review: I bow at the knee of Michael Connelly and anxiously await each and every new release. This book of short stories is perfect for "tiding me over" till that happens. Mr Connelly never fails to please me although this book would naturally satisfy me more if the stories were not quite as short as they are here. Still, they are as tightly composed as his longer books and I will be content, mostly, until the next new book is in my hands.

demonstrations.item_text:
Murder Mile: A Jane Tennison Thriller (Book 4)
Kindle Edition

Prime Suspect meets Ashes to Ashes as we see Jane Tennison starting out on her police career . The fourth in the bestselling Jane Tennison thrillers, MURDER MILE is set at the height of the 'Winter of Discontent'. Can Jane Tennison uncover a serial killer? February, 1979, 'The Winter of Discontent'. Economic chaos has led to widespread strikes across Britain. Jane Tennison, now a Detective Sergeant, has been posted to Peckham Criminal Investigation Department, one of London's toughest areas. As the rubbish on the streets begins to pile up, so does the murder count: two bodies in as many days. There are no suspects and the manner of death is different in each case. The only link between the two victims is the location of the bodies, found within a short distance of each other near Rye Lane in Peckham. Three days later another murder occurs in the same area. Press headlines scream that a serial killer is loose on 'Murder Mile' and that police incompetence is hampering the investigation. Jane is under immense pressure to catch the killer before they strike again. Working long hours with little sleep, what she uncovers leaves her doubting her own mind.
demonstrations.review: I have enjoyed the Tennison series written and filmed about her later career in the London police force but this is part of a series which takes place early on in her life there. She’s a force in her own right that the generally male group of detectives struggle to adjust to in Murder Mile. They appear to do that in this book but we discover that they may or may not do so. Read this and find out for yourself.

demonstrations.item_text:
The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo (Millennium Series)
Hardcover – Deckle Edge, September 16, 2008

A sensation across Europe—millions of copies soldA spellbinding amalgam of murder mystery, family saga, love story, and financial intrigue.It’s about the disappearance forty years ago of Harriet Vanger, a young scion of one of the wealthiest families in Sweden . . . and about her octogenarian uncle, determined to know the truth about what he believes was her murder.It’s about Mikael Blomkvist, a crusading journalist recently at the wrong end of a libel case, hired to get to the bottom of Harriet’s disappearance . . . and about Lisbeth Salander, a twenty-four-year-old pierced and tattooed genius hacker possessed of the hard-earned wisdom of someone twice her age—and a terrifying capacity for ruthlessness to go with it—who assists Blomkvist with the investigation. This unlikely team discovers a vein of nearly unfathomable iniquity running through the Vanger family, astonishing corruption in the highest echelons of Swedish industrialism—and an unexpected connection between themselves.It’s a contagiously exciting, stunningly intelligent novel about society at its most hidden, and about the intimate lives of a brilliantly realized cast of characters, all of them forced to face the darker aspects of their world and of their own lives.
demonstrations.review:
The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo, written by the late Steig Larsson starts slowly but increases drama and speed as two story lines build in parallel time.
The heiress to a wealthy, seriously dysfunctional family's money has disappeared thirty years previously when she was a young teen. Her uncle still has doubts about her probable murder and wangles a way to put a journalist on the job, finding any information on the seriously cold case. The journalist has quite recently lost his reputation and has to spend three months in jail for a crime that is unclear to me. What has happened is that the author has lost a bitter court battle with the evil Wennerstrom, an important Swedish businessman.
The parallel character is the eponymous girl with the tattoo, an intriguingly disaffected young woman who is kept in legal thrall, again for reasons that I fail to understand. The Swedish legalities and financial mazes aren't familiar to me but are important to the story, so I muddle through without fully comprehending the ins and outs of the laws. Nevermind, it matters not enough to prevent the reader from following the story, becoming totally involved in the outcome.
The English translation is awkward in places but is honest and understandable. That and the Swedish legal system won't stop us from this fascinating thrill ride!

demonstrations.item_text:
Spirit of Steamboat: A Walt Longmire Story

A Christmas novella for fans of the hit drama series LONGMIRE now on Netflix and the New York Times –bestselling series. Craig Johnson's new novel , The Western Star, will be available from Viking in Fall 2017. Sheriff Walt Longmire is in his office reading A Christmas Carol when he is interrupted by a ghost of Christmas past: a young woman with a hairline scar and more than a few questions about his predecessor, Lucian Connally. With his daughter Cady and undersherrif Moretti otherwise engaged, Walt’s on his own this Christmas Eve, so he agrees to help her. At the Durant Home for Assisted Living, Lucian is several tumblers into his Pappy Van Winkle’s and swears he’s never clapped eyes on the woman before. Disappointed, she whispers “Steamboat” and begins a story that takes them all back to Christmas Eve 1988—a story that will thrill and delight the bestselling series’ devoted fans.
demonstrations.review: As a dedicated Craig Johnson fan, this little dividend was a pleasant surprise. It was an "edge of your seat" read even though the outcome was never in doubt. CJ must have done a whole lot of research to pull this one off as well as he did! Keep them coming, please!

demonstrations.item_text:
The Late Show (Renee Ballard Book 1)
Kindle Edition

In this first installment of the Renée Ballard series, #1 bestselling author Michael Connelly introduces a "complicated and driven" young detective fighting to prove herself on the LAPD's toughest beat ( The New York Times ). Renee Ballard works the midnight shift in Hollywood, beginning many investigations but finishing few, as each morning she turns everything over to the daytime units. It's a frustrating job for a once up-and-coming detective, but it's no accident. She's been given this beat as punishment after filing a sexual harassment complaint against a supervisor.But one night Ballard catches two assignments she doesn't want to part with. First, a prostitute is brutally beaten and left for dead in a parking lot. All signs point to a crime of premeditation, not passion, by someone with big evil on his mind. Then she sees a young waitress breathe her last after being caught up in a nightclub shooting. Though dubbed a peripheral victim, the waitress buys Ballard a way in, and this time she is determined not to give up at dawn. Against orders and her partner's wishes, she works both cases by day while maintaining her shift by night. As the investigations intertwine, Ballard is forced to face her own demons and confront a danger she could never have imagined. To find justice for these victims who can't speak for themselves, she must put not only her career but her life on the line. Propulsive as a jolt of adrenaline and featuring a bold and defiant new heroine, The Late Show is yet more proof that Michael Connelly is "a master of the genre" ( Washington Post ).
demonstrations.review: Michael Connelly has to be at the top of my personal list of favorite authors. When I started reading The Late Show, my initial reaction was that it seemed to be a sort of instruction manual on police rules and regulations for those readers who hadn't stayed awake during previous classes, but that didn't last long I soon woke up myself and became involved with Renee Ballard and Lola her canine sidekick. I loved them and their whole convoluted story. It's hard for some readers to change loyalties to various characters but I do hope others will take a chance on Ballard and enjoy them as much as I do. This is a great new addition to my complete Connelly collection.

demonstrations.item_text:
The Long and Faraway Gone: A Novel
Kindle Edition

WINNER OF THE EDGAR AWARD, THE MACAVITY AWARD, THE ANTHONY AWARD, AND THE BARRY AWARD FOR BEST PAPERBACK ORIGINAL NOMINATED FOR THE 2015 LA TIMES BOOK PRIZE With the compelling narrative tension and psychological complexity of the works of Laura Lippman, Dennis Lehane, Kate Atkinson, and Michael Connelly, Edgar Award-nominee Lou Berney’s The Long and Faraway Gone is a smart, fiercely compassionate crime story that explores the mysteries of memory and the impact of violence on survivors—and the lengths they will go to find the painful truth of the events that scarred their lives. In the summer of 1986, two tragedies rocked Oklahoma City. Six movie-theater employees were killed in an armed robbery, while one inexplicably survived. Then, a teenage girl vanished from the annual State Fair. Neither crime was ever solved. Twenty-five years later, the reverberations of those unsolved cases quietly echo through survivors’ lives. A private investigator in Vegas, Wyatt’s latest inquiry takes him back to a past he’s tried to escape—and drags him deeper into the harrowing mystery of the movie house robbery that left six of his friends dead. Like Wyatt, Julianna struggles with the past—with the day her beautiful older sister Genevieve disappeared. When Julianna discovers that one of the original suspects has resurfaced, she’ll stop at nothing to find answers. As Wyatt's case becomes more complicated and dangerous, and Julianna seeks answers from a ghost, their obsessive quests not only stir memories of youth and first love, but also begin to illuminate dark secrets of the past. But will their shared passion and obsession heal them, or push them closer to the edge? Even if they find the truth, will it help them understand what happened, that long and faraway gone summer? Will it set them free—or ultimately destroy them?
demonstrations.review:
This excellent book manages to braid two different threads of two stories featuring two main characters during different time periods, primarily in Oklahoma City. The set-up occurs in the mid 80's and it flashes forward to the present day. The author deftly handles the plot shifts and the times admirably. I was quite comfortable with his ability to juggle them.
I loved the book and didn't want to put it down. It's a crime novel with a few mystery elements, but I wouldn't characterize it as pure mystery.

In this beautifully illustrated natural history that links extinct larger feline species with those still in existence, collaborators Alan Turner and Mauricio Anton weave together the evidence of modern feline behavior with that of the fossil record. target.review: but that does't make his book bad. He had some very interesting theories that helped my write my final paper on feline evolution. I would recomment it to students as well as professionals because the concepts are certainly well thought, but stated in an easy to read manner
