demonstrations.item_text:
Mastering Macro Photography - Ideas, Tips, Tutorials & DIY Equipment

Learn macro photography tips and techniques to become a master macro photographer. Do you want to learn macro photography but don’t know where to start? Or are you frustrated because your macro photos are average looking no matter what you do? If this sounds familiar, then this book is for you. Unlike other books, this book is not about showing you pages of beautiful macro photos. The main purpose of the book is to equip you with the right knowledge to help you to become a better macro photographer . It will put the focus on the important skills that you need to develop in order to transform into a master macro photographer. For the macro photography beginner, you will learn how to get started in macro photography by understanding the basics. This includes – •Learning what macro photography is about and how it is different to close-up photography •Discovering the type of macro photographer that you are as this will dictate the type of photos that you should be taking •Knowing what macro photography equipment you REALLY need and how to choose the right macro photography gear •Understanding the importance of depth of field and how to control it •Helping you to develop the macro photographer’s mindset Unfortunately, many people do not try macro photography because they think macro photography is expensive and that they need a macro lens. If this is you, this book will dispel that myth and show you some of the lesser known ways to get started in macro photography! This book will even guide you through step by step on making your own macro photography equipment. So why spend the money when you can make your own equipment? If you are a macro photographer who is struggling to capture great macro photos, this book will help you to understand the common problems in macro photography so that you can avoid them. You will discover how to identify the type of blur in your macro photos and learn tips and techniques to achieve tack sharp photos . We will also introduce you to the ‘Focus Stacking’ technique that is used by many advance macro photographers to extend the depth of field in their macro photos. To further help you capture better macro photos, we highlight what you need to consider before pressing the shutter button . By adhering to some basic color harmony and composition principles you can take your macro photos to the next level. A minor adjustment to how you currently photograph could make a big difference to all your future macro photos. Being macro photographers ourselves, we know you love to photograph insects and flowers. That’s why we have dedicated a whole section in this book to share practical macro photography tips and tricks on photographing insects and flowers . And if there are no insects or flowers around you, we have you covered. In the book, we share some of our favorite places to find macro photography subjects. For those who are interested, we will even give you tips on how to transform your garden into a magnet for macro photography subjects! As you know, there will be times when you just run out of macro photography ideas. As such, we have shared the very best and unique macro photography tutorials with you . So for times when you just don’t know what to shoot, just try one of the unique macro photography ideas. All you need to do is to follow the step by step tutorial covering what is required, the camera settings to use and other creative ideas to try in order to spice things up. If you are keen to master macro photography quickly, then you will need ‘Mastering Macro Photography – Ideas, Tips, Tutorials & DIY Equipment’ by your side. The journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step, so buy this book and start seeing in macro!
demonstrations.review:
Sometimes a book can be too "basic". Which seems to be the case with much of this book. Also, too much time is spent on homemade equipment. For instance a flash diffuser involves cutting up a Coke (R) can and a milk jug to make a flash diffuser. Just a simple piece of plastic wrapped around the flash will do. The making of an extension tube from a Pringles (R) can. Better and sturdier extension tubes can be made of PVC pipe or heavy cardboard shipping tubes and mounts purchased off Amazon or ebay for a few bucks or scavenged from dead cameras or lenses. Anyway real extension tubes can be bought from the same sources for about the same cost. I'm not knocking making your own equipment, as the experience can be rewarding. I have made pinhole cameras (one with a Polaroid back), electronic flashes, and 8 x 10 glass plate negatives.
Also in the bubble section, glycerin is described as a sweetener. No, glycerin an ingredient in hand lotions and medicines. Corn syrup is a sweetener and works in the bubble recipe. It seems as some research was too hasty, as most recipes for longer lived bubbles use either one. Both are viscous liquids to make tougher bubbles. A few typos, such as one page refers to the "shuttle" (sic) several times on the page. Too heavy a reliance on spell checker and editing programs, I think.
All in all the book seems hastily put together and relies too much on research and not hands-on.
But then I will highly recommend this book as a starter book for macro and close up photography. It covers a lot of basic information, for instance the section on photo stacking is excellent. I get the feeling that the author has actually done this.
The section on lenses and cameras is good. I would like to add that Nikon calls it's macro lenses "micro" lenses.

demonstrations.review:
I bought two of these, one for my photo bag, the Used one. The used one was new, the pages never relaxed.
Another New one for my library.

demonstrations.item_text:
Photographing the Unseen World: Art and Techniques
Paperback – April 20, 2020

For the first time of its invention, photography has been used to visualize events that are either too fast or too slow for the eye to perceive, or subjects that are outside the spectral range of the human eye. This book shows how you can photograph a range of subjects and see the world as never before. Written with clear and accessible text, it explores and suggests techniques that expose new images in new ways, and pushes the boundaries of the photographer's creative potential. Techniques include: ultraviolet (UV) and infrared (IR) photography; high speed and time-lapse photography; close-up, macro and photography with the aid of a microscope and finally, photography using polarized light. Most of the techniques are accessible to all photographers using readily available equipment (UV and IR will require some specialist items), and have been relatively unexplored so give the adventurous photographer great potential to experiment and produce unique images.
demonstrations.review:
If you are just starting in macro, close up, IR or UV, this is your class 101. It answers your questions, even those you don't know to ask yet.
It covers cameras, even some older cameras that you can buy cheap Nikon D40 and Nikon D70 that will work well in IR without being converted, you just need a filter.
It's coverage of filters is comprehensive. It defines filter terminology, such as band pass, cut on, cut off, hot mirror, etc.
It covers the gear you will need.
It covers both the scientific and artistic aspects of this type of photography.
The images illustrate the text and are not meant to be artistic or represent his best work. It is not a coffee-table book.
His other book "Digital Ultraviolet and Infrared Photography" is for mature photographers, that is professionals working in the scientific, forensics, medical, etc. field.. This book, 'Photographing the Unseen World" is your first book. You many never need another.
I highly recommend this book. I could have saved a lot of money on buying how-to books had I had this book first.

demonstrations.review:
Get Davies book in the mail. Spend the next hour going through it.
As usual for Adrian Davies, the book delivers a great deal of information, always illustrated with beautiful photos.
I had never heard of the Burrens in County Claire on the west coast of Ireland. The grykes between the clints contain a great many Alpine flowers growing at sea level.
The book is as much an environmental study as a text book. From fire ravaged landscapes to using a flatbed scanner to make digital images of flowers and plants.
As usual with a Davies book, there is no fluff. It is all good solid information. From cameras and equipment to technique and post processing, this book delivers.

target.item_text:
Sweet
Hardcover – June 2, 2015

The luxurious celebrity cruise launching the trendy new diet sweetener Solu should be the vacation of a lifetime. But Laurel is starting to regret accepting her friend Viv's invitation. She's already completely embarrassed herself in front of celebrity host Tom Forelli―the hottest guy ever!―and she's too sick to even try the sweetener. And that's before Viv and all the other passengers start acting really strange. Tom knows that he should be grateful for this job and the chance to shed his former-child-star image. His publicists have even set up a 'romance' with a sexy reality star. But as things on the ship start to get wild, he finds himself drawn to a different girl. And when the hosting gig turns into an expose on the shocking side effects of Solu, it's Laurel that he's determined to save.Emmy Laybourne, author of the Monument 14 trilogy, takes readers on a dream vacation in Sweet that goes first comically, then tragically, then horrifyingly , wrong!
target.review:
To the point: This book was good. It went to all the places you wanted it to go and was a very satisfying read.

Review: This books starts out with a down to earth character who is confident in her life and who she is. So obviously she doesn't buy into the hype of this new sugar replacement that also helps you lose weight dramatically. She's there to support her friend and she does a great job of this. The cruise is over the top gorgeous and amazing. There is a mix of the most famous celebrities and the richest families around and everyone is having a blast.

Unfortunately there's a twist. Things get crazy. And this book really takes it there. I almost felt it was a little comedic. I didn't take it as horrific as it was supposed to be. It reminded me of a scary B movie, the plot is there but the acting is terrible. I don't know about you but I actually love it. There's nothing realistic about this book, not even the character's reactions to the twisted events. I don't know but I'd imagine I would be absolutely terrified and not just walking around crazy people. I'd be getting away, the first day.

The end was ABRUPT. I would have loved to see the characters dealing with the aftermath. But that would have made it too serious and like I said there was something very silly and comedic about the way the characters acted. So although I think the book was fun I gave it a 3 stars because it was just a little too impractical and unrealistic (at least in the way the characters react to the drama).

I recommend this book to anyone who loves a little humor in their sci-fi horror stories!

Sweet by Emmy Laybourne. Feiwel & Friends (June 2, 2015). 288 pages. Science Fiction/Survival/Addiction. I received this copy from a Goodreads giveaway.

from www.amandanicolebooks.wordpress.com

demonstrations.item_text:
Captive
Paperback – March 24, 2015

He's the most dangerous man she's ever met…and she's falling in love with him. Madison Frost is desperate to escape her life. Daughter of a prominent businessman, she has everything a girl could ask for. Except for a family who's present in her life, and anyone to talk to outside the four walls of the prison she calls home. Madison dreams of one day leaving her life behind. She never thought being kidnapped is how it would happen.Now she's being held captive by a man who's as frightening as he is sinfully gorgeous. Enormous, muscular, and filled with secrets, the man they call Ghost is an enigmatic mercenary, and Madison is trapped with him. She doesn't know who hired him or why, but the more time she spends at his mercy, the more she realizes he's not what he seems. Beneath his rough exterior lies an unexpected gentleness and a heart as broken and battered as her own.But as Madison lets down her walls, Ghost holds tight to his, hiding secrets that could destroy everything. "A vulnerable but indomitable heroine and a hero who will haunt your dreams long after the last page. Raw, sexy and unexpectedly tender, Captive is a powerful, gripping story." ―Kit Rocha, New York Times Bestselling Author "With character so real I feel like I've known them all my life…a pure, sweet, hot romance. It's a must read!"― M. Leighton, New York Times Bestselling Author on Caged In Winter
demonstrations.review:
I loved this book. It was fun and full of those difficult moments that really make you stress out for the characters. Madison's life is tough which reminds us the beauty and money really isn't everything. This part almost felt realistic because there are so many stories about wealthy families plagued with neglect, abuse, mental illness and substance abuse. Madison is such a lovely character, she has this deep awareness and ability to understand people, possibly because of her troubled home life. She has a lot of compassion and even more she is emotionally strong. I got the sense she could handle any situation.

I grew up saying "When someone does something terrible you have to wonder how awful things must have been for them to turn around and do terrible things" because my mother always said "good people do bad things sometimes and that doesn't make them bad people it just means they need help". Now let's be clear, I'm not talking about sociopaths or people with mental illnesses that cause them to lack consideration of living things and are absent of natural emotions. Some people are just bad. But this book felt like a little reminder of my bringing up.

I didn't think I would like a love story between a kidnapper and a "victim" but c'mon doesn't every female have that fantasy? A young handsome strong man stealing them away from the rest of the world and showing her a kind, soft side that he doesn't show anyone.. Yes, I could get into that.

I gave this book 5 stars because it completely surprised me and despite my efforts not to, I fell for all of the characters! I looked the plot and Walsh's writing style is magical and captivating (pun intended?). But seriously, I love an author who can make a story flow so well that I can't find a comfortable spot to put it down and I need to finish the book in one night. Which means I face the consequences of way too energetic babies way too early in the morning. The punishment is worth it!

This book has mature content so I recommend it to steamy-loving adults. It's a great Romance novel and anyone craving a little dreamy love would adore this book!

So I really loved the book and since I bought one I actually won another copy and thought this was the perfect opportunity to spread the love!

Giveaway on www.amandanicolebooks.wordpress.com

Luckiest Girl Alive: A Novel
Hardcover – May 12, 2015

***AN INSTANT NEW YORK TIMES AND USA TODAY BESTSELLER*** Fans of Gone Girl and The Girl on the Train will thrill at “the perfect page-turner to start your summer” ( People , Book of the Week): Luckiest Girl Alive —described by Reese Witherspoon as “one of those reads you just can’t put down!” “ Loved Gone Girl ? demonstrations.review:
To the point: I LOVED this book! I haven't read Gone Girl, or The Girl on the Train so I didn't have a comparison. I had no idea what the book would be like and the surprise was awesome. Great book, check it out.

Review: This book attacked me. Seriously, I did not expect any of the events that unfolded to occur and even after one crazy event was leaked there were still more secrets to reveal. I couldn't believe what I was reading, a book so bold and so realistic. Absolutely crazy with drama and somehow still so relatable. This book haunts me and I couldn't sleep after finishing it. It's amazing that a book could reach me so deeply.

In the beginning I got the impression this would be some melodramatic drama of a woman realizing how boring her life is and she needed more. Honestly, I drudge through the first few pages my excitement wearing thing because I thought I knew the rest of the plotline already. But I was wrong, there is no romance. There is no love in this story. It's horrific. You probably think I'm overdoing this but this book has brought be to the darkest depths of my fears and played it out with so much description that I could easily image the scenarios happening.

If you read this book, it will eat you alive. Prepare yourself my friend, because once you read the words and paint the story in your brain it will replay like on a movie screen and you won't be able to get it out of your head. That's why I give it 5 stars. I love realistic. I love the psychologically tortured and I love to watch their journey. The darker it gets the more I need to read and once I start I need to know the ending. The ending, the furthest from realistic to me because of how easily people can just go the wrong way and the confrontation - well I don't believe many women would handle that confrontation or those words the way Ani did. But as I remember quickly, how everyone treated her, family, "friends" and everyone in between - that was wholly realistic to me and this quickly saddened me about the state of understanding and women oppression in our society.

Terrifyingly amazing, I recommend this book to anyone who can handle it. It is deep and dark and twisty. What makes it so scary is how realistic it is. This isn't some paranormal, sci-fi, fantasy that we can tell ourselves isn't real at the end. This stuff happens. It happens to people just like us.

Jessica Knoll is one hell of an author. I'm absolutely terrified to follow her career but am already addicted to her direction and plot and will most likely grab any book she writes, with a box of tissues and some bad tasting polish to keep me from shredding my nails next time.

Luckiest Girl Alive by Jessica Knoll. Simon & Schuster (May 12, 2015). 352 pages. Fiction: New Adult, Drama, Suspense. I received this copy from the publisher and want to thank them for the opportunity to review this exciting book!

demonstrations.item_text:
The Redemption of Callie & Kayden
Paperback – February 11, 2014

From the New York Times bestselling author of The Coincidence of Callie & Kayden comes an emotional new story about two troubled souls sharing one all-encompassing love . . . The dark secret Kayden has kept hidden for years is finally out. Worse, he's facing charges for battery. The only way to clear his name is for Callie to speak up-something he'll never ask her to do. Instead, he'll do whatever he must to protect her . . . even if it means letting go of the only girl he's ever loved. Callie knows Kayden is going back to his dark place and desperately wants to save him. But that means facing her greatest fear and admitting her own painful secrets aloud. The thought of breaking her silence terrifies her-but not as much as the thought of losing Kayden forever. Deep in her heart, Callie knows the time has come for her and Kayden to forget the pain of the past. With the help of her friends Seth and Luke she makes a plan to show Kayden the life they could have. But can she convince him they can make a fresh start together-or is she already too late?
demonstrations.review:
To the point: This book solidified my love for Jessica Sorensen's writing and her characters Callie and Kayden.

Review: WOW, this sequel to The Coincidence of Callie and Kayden blew my mind! The way all the traumas unfold really worked perfectly for me. I felt a lot of the pain resolve for me slowly and the struggle between the characters and their pasts really caused a lot of friction for me. This friction kept me hooked and I begged for the characters to make it through this rough time. I was already addicted to their story at this point and I felt them regress back into their pain, I cried and laughed out loud and basically felt every human emotion possible.

The plot was almost as perfect as the first book. The ending was more solid with this book where it feels like I don't NEED to read the next book (even though I want to). I felt great about how the story went and I really cheered for Callie and Kayden, as well as their friends and family that I came to love as well.

I gave this book 5 stars because the writing is flawless, the plot will engulf your mind and emotions and the characters have amazing complexity and emotional depth. I'm excited to read the next book and will write a review quickly of course. I think this is a great trilogy for romance lovers, new adult ages and a little bit of psychological and sociological drama.

The Redemption of Callie and Kayden by Jessica Sorensen. Forever; Reprint edition (February 11, 2014). 416 pages. NA Romance, Contemporary. I purchased my own copy and decided to write an honest review.

demonstrations.item_text:
The Coincidence of Callie & Kayden
Paperback – August 6, 2013

From the bestselling author of The Secret of Ella and Micha comes a mesmerizing novel of fate, friendship, and the healing power of love . . . The Coincidence of Callie & Kayden For Kayden, suffering in silence was the only way to survive. If he was lucky, he could keep his head down, do as he was told, and make it through the day. But one night it seemed like his luck-and his life-might finally end . . . until an angel named Callie appeared just in time to rescue him. Callie has never believed in luck. Not since her twelfth birthday when everything was taken from her. After the worst was over, she locked up her feelings and vowed never to tell anyone what happened. Now, six years later, she continues to struggle with the painful secret that threatens to consume her. When fate lands Kayden and Callie at the same college, Kayden is determined to get to know the beautiful girl who changed his destiny. Quiet and reserved, Callie still fears letting anyone else into her world. But Kayden is certain that Callie has come back into his life for a reason. And the more he tries to be a part of her life, the more he realizes that, this time, it's Callie who needs to be saved . . .
demonstrations.review:
To the point: I fell in love with this NA romance and really enjoyed watching the characters grow!

Review: I instantly fell in love with Jessica Sorensen's writing style. It flows beautifully and effortlessly, making reading a breeze - which allowed me to suck this story up in a matter of hours. The language is poetic and the plot is absolutely perfect. I really kept guessing about what would happen next and clenching my heart in fear of what could happen next.

Callie is an amazing character! She's extremely relatable and very realistic. I felt her pain, my heart broke and at the same time I pulled for her, I needed her to heal! I felt anger towards her family as she felt pain and although I wished they would just open their eyes, I know how common it is for victims and families to be disconnected and crimes to go unknown for so long. Kayden is such a broken sweet soul. I really wanted him to be okay, my heart broke for him as I can imagine how often this is the story for other teens around the country. I desperately wanted these two characters to help each other.

The plot goes amazingly and I quickly snatched up the next book, The Redemption of Callie and Kayden, and finished it before the day ended. I think this book couldn't be improved and I don't have any critiques. I recommend this book to anyone looking for a romance story that's going to hit you hard and deep.

The Coincidence of Callie and Kayden by Jessica Sorensen. Forever (August 6, 2013). 400 pages. NA Fiction, Contemporary, Romance. I purchased this copy myself and provided an honest review.

demonstrations.item_text: Button Man
demonstrations.review: While the ending is somewhat far-fetched, overall this is an excellent novel about Depression Era Jewish business owners' struggle with gangsters and union thugs.  As seems to be currently fashionable, the story combines fictional characters with historical figures and events. The result of this mashup, is an easy to read, very entertaining story with believable characters and a plausible plot.

demonstrations.item_text:
The French Foreign Legion: A Complete History of the Legendary Fighting Force

“Unparalleled in the thoughtfulness and detail of its coverage.”— The Washington Post The French Foreign Legion is a complete, captivating study of the famed fighting force, from its inception in 1831 to modern times. Historian Douglas Porch chronicles the Legion’s involvement in Spain, Mexico, Indochina, Madagascar, WWI, Vietnam, and Algiers (to name a few) and delves into the inner workings of legionnaires and their captains. demonstrations.review: Anyone looking for an exciting, glamourous, romantic recitation of Foreign Legion history should look elsewhere.  This is a well written, well researched and exhaustive history of the French Foreign Legion for military academics and historians.

demonstrations.item_text: The Cali Cartel: Beyond Narcos
demonstrations.review: This is a very informative book for anyone with an interest in the Cali Cartel or international drug trafficking. The author believes that the DEA, CIA and George W. Bush were in cahoots with the Cali Cartel and earlier with Pablo Escobar to raise money for anti-guerilla activities.  However, he confines those opinions to last two chapters of the book.  The rest of the book is a straight forward, carefully researched history of the Cali Cartel, devoid of bias and opinion.

demonstrations.item_text:
Read This if You Want to Take Great Photographs
Kindle Edition

Photography is now more popular than ever thanks to the rapid development of digital cameras. Read This If You Want to Take Great Photographs is ideal for this new wave of snapshooters using DSLR, compact system and bridge cameras. It contains no graphs, no techie diagrams and no camera-club jargon. Instead, it inspires readers through iconic images and playful copy, packed with hands-on tips. Split into five sections, the book covers composition, exposure, light, lenses and the art of seeing. Masterpieces by acclaimed photographers – including Henri Cartier-Bresson, Sebastião Salgado, Fay Godwin, Nadav Kander, Daido Moriyama and Martin Parr – serve to illustrate points and encourage readers to try out new ideas. Today’s aspiring photographers want immediacy and see photography as an affordable way of expressing themselves quickly and creatively. This handbook meets their needs, teaching them how to take photographs using professional techniques.
demonstrations.review: This book explains the basics of taking photographs, how the camera and photographer become a team to make a photograph that people will actually want to see. The author begins by explaining how the camera and lens work and them he discusses what the role of the photographer is to make the photo. All this is done in lay terms without long technical dissertations. This is a very good book for beginning photographers who want to move beyond taking snapshots. It is a very short book and I would have preferred a more detailed discussion and more examples to study, but overall I think the author nailed it.

demonstrations.item_text:
Nikon D810 (Expanded Guides)
Paperback – May 15, 2015

Nikon’s high-end 36MP D800 and D800E DSLRs have been consolidated with the release of the D810. It is not simply an upgrade: major changes substantially extend its capabilities and make the camera more attractive to buyers considering a move to a full-frame camera.  Some features from the D4s have been incorporated into the D810. Videographers, for example, will be pleased with additions to its video feature set. Other refinements include a redesigned shutter and mirror mechanism to reduce the shock of shutter actuation, which can reduce resolution. There’s also a new S-Raw mode for reduced-resolution raw capture.
demonstrations.review: This is an excellent guide to the Nikon D810 and it is far superior to the little book that came with the camera. The book itself is very nicely printed with clear instructions, photos and drawings.  I think it's a good investment.

demonstrations.item_text:
Bomb the Suburbs

Should graffiti writers organize to tear up the cities, or should they really be bombing the ?burbs? Thats the question posed by William Upski Wimsatt in his seminal foray into the world of hip-hop, rap, and street art, and the culture and politics that surround it. But to say that the book deals only with taggers and hip-hop is selling it short. Taking on a broad range of topics, including suburban sprawl, racial identity, and youth activism, Wimsatt (a graffiti artist himself) uses a kaleidoscopic approach that combines stories, cartoons, interviews, disses, parodies, and original research to challenge the suburban mindset wherever its found: suburbs and corporate headquarters, inner cities and housing projects, even in hip-hop itself. Funny, provocative, and painfully honest, Bomb the Suburbs encourages readers to expand their social boundaries and explore the vibrant, chaotic world that exists beyond their comfort zones.
demonstrations.review: hip hop is a cult. if you're not a practicing member of this cult then you probably won't enjoy this book. if you're not from chicago then you'll probably enjoy it even less. it's very local. i like Upski (he uses his brain!), but this book just wasn't that good. i didn't like the part about bombing the rich suburban areas. i think there should be a place where people can expect to elevate to without being forced to be bombarded with graffiti. graffiti is for cities. it looks stupid and out of place in the suburbs. just cuz Upski likes the cities and loathes the suburbs does not mean everybody else shares that view. people are presently free to live wherever they want (if they can afford it) and if they want to move away from the ghetto they shouldn't be bullied into having the ghetto brought to them.

target.item_text:

target.review:
The quality you expect from Autocourse. Fillied with fantastic pictures from the 2003 Chap Car season. Each race is detailed with results and behind the scenes information.

But the pictures are what really steals the show here. Huge color closeup of the cars and the drivers as well.

I can't say enough good things about this book. I really enjoy getting this book each year.

demonstrations.item_text:
A Twist of the Wrist Vol. 2: The Basics of High-Performance Motorcycle Riding
Paperback – August 31, 1997

Straight facts about riding! A Twist of the Wrist, the acknowledged number one book on rider improvement for ten years straight, brought riders worldwide to a new understanding of vital riding skills. Uncovers and traces, action by action, the direct links between man and machine.
demonstrations.review:
As a beginning rider that completed the MSF riding course, I was searching for the tools that would allow me to ride faster and safer. While the MSF covers the "how to" it doesn't really go into the "why"...This book does an excellent job of telling you why you do things on the bike and how the bike will react.
If you are a street rider wanting to ride faster, better and safer than skip "Twist of the Wrist" and buy this book instead. "Twist II" really should have been the first book in this series as it focuses on fundamentals, while "Twist" emphasizes the skills of road racing, which are obviously different than street riding.
While the information contained in this book will always be relevant, the text and layout look a bit dated, especially in this day and age of "...for Dummies" books. The text is easy to read and comprehend but can be a bit juvenile at times.
I have read and applied the concepts of this book to my everyday riding and feel it has accelerated my learning curve tremendously over what I would have learned simply by doing or listing to the advice of friends.
Bottom line: 95% of riders can benefit from reading this book. Read it, apply it and be a better rider.

demonstrations.item_text:

demonstrations.review:
If you've never worked on a bike before this is a good book to start your journey. It goes over all of the adjustments and maintenance items you will need to pay attention to on your bike.
Downside is that a good portion of the bike technology they cover is no longer standard equipment on current bikes. This isn't enough of a problem to not recommend the book however. And could actually be useful if you pick up an older used bike that you want to get back in operating condition.
Excellent graphics and easy to read directions make this a solid choice for the beginning bike mechanic. One note: You will need a few bike specific tools to work on your steed.

Excellent design & Layout
Easy to understand
Comprehensive

Comprehensive
rag paper pages

Eben Weiss, aka Bike Snob NYC, is the voice of cyclists everywhere. Through his popular blog he has been informing, entertaining, and critiquing the bike-riding community since 2007. With his latest book, The Ultimate Bicycle Owner's Manual , Weiss makes his vast experience and practical advice available to bike "newbies" and veterans alike. Chapters cover Obtaining a Bike, Understanding Your Bike, Maintaining Your Bike, Operating Your Bike, Off-Road Riding, Coexisting with Drivers, Competitive Cycling, Bike Travel, Cycling with Kids, and What the Future Holds for Bikes in our Communities. Weiss's humorous, down-to-earth style takes all the mystery and intimidation out of cycling and will inspire even the most hesitant couch potato to get out and ride! Eben Weiss is the blogger behind Bike Snob NYC. He is the author of Bike Snob , Bike Snob Abroad , and The Enlightened Cyclist. He lives in New York City with his family.
demonstrations.review:
When I saw that there was going to be yet another book on how to buy/own/repair a bike I thought how could anyone need another book on this topic.
But when I saw who the author was, there was a sliver of sunlight through my decidedly overcast view of the subject matter.

Once I received the book and dug in I was really pleasantly surprised. The Snob not only brings his unique wit (sarcasm) and common sense approach to all things cycling but molds them into useful advice and commentary for someone new or returning to bikes.

Succinctly answering the questions as to why you shouldn't buy a department store bike, why you should care what materiel your bike is made of and other sage advice about why helmets really aren't that important to your safety. All with an overarching sense of humor that is his trademark.

If you are interested in getting into bikes for the first time or returning as a middle age warrior after years off this book is the perfect place to start. Don't buy a bike without reading this first.

demonstrations.item_text:

Championship Winning Race Bikes and the World Superbike Girls! The top factory race bikes of the SBK World and AMA National Superbike Championships, photographed together the beautiful FastDates.com SBK trophy girls. demonstrations.review:
Year after year this calendar never looses its appeal. Sold worldwide and featuring some of the most exotic racing machinery in existance. The cover features actress Delilah Stombs and Penthouse Pet of the year Zdenka Podkapova looking fantastic aboard Troy Bayliss' Ducati 998F. And lets not forget Miss Great Britain Nicki Lane. demonstrations.item_text:
Harley Davidson Rolling Sculpture
Hardcover – January 1, 1998

There can be little argument that Harley-Davidson has become an American legend-one that is known the world over. But the company can also be heralded as a survivor. Two world wars, the Great Depression, and the fickle buying trends of the American public managed to kill off all of the estimated 300 U.S. motorcycle manufacturers that once dotted the country-every one of them-except for Harley-Davidson. This volume celebrates Harley-Davidson's 95 years in the motorcycle business. The Motor Company has come a long way since William Harley and Arthur and Walter Davidson pieced together that first prototype and no doubt the founders would be proud of its progress.
demonstrations.review:
Excellent book for the beginning enthusiast. Fantastic dust jacket looks like it was chromed at the factory.
Great pictures with basic descripions and history of the brand.
Sure there are better books but this is a good one to start with or as a gift.

target.item_text:
Night's Child: A Detective Murdoch Mystery (Murdoch Mysteries Book 5)
Kindle Edition

After thirteen-year-old Agnes Fisher faints at school, her teacher, the young and still idealistic Amy Slade, is shocked to discover in the girl’s desk two stereoscopic photographs. One is of a dead baby in its cradle, and on the back Agnes has scrawled a terrible message. Worse, the other photograph is of Agnes in a pose captioned “What Mr. Newly Wed Really Wants.” When Agnes doesn’t show up at school the next day, her teacher takes the two photographs to the police. Murdoch, furious at the sexual exploitation of such a young girl, resolves to find the photographer – and to put him behind bars. Night’s Child is the fifth novel in Maureen Jennings’s highly praised historical mystery series. Three of Jennings’s novels have been made into TV movies under the title Murder 19C: The Murdoch Mysteries . Bravo/CHUM is currently developing a series based on the character of Detective William Murdoch for broadcast in 2007.
target.review: Wow, Night's Child is an impressive historical mystery starring Detective Murdoch.  The plot is excellent while the characters are rich in depth.  This book is the fifth novel in the series and I would recommend reading them all.

demonstrations.item_text:
Easy Microsoft Office 2010 (Que's Easy Series)
1st Edition

Describes the fundamentals of Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excell, PowerPoint, Outlook, and OneNote, and highlights each application's new features.
demonstrations.review:
The book advertises - "No need to feel intimidated-we'll hold your hand every step of the way". LOL, I wish someone was holding my hand because no matter how effective a book is written, Office 2010 will not be considered easy.

With all of that in mind, I would recommend this book for people who learn best by reading instructions. If you are not of that learning type then you may be disappointed. If you do well with written instructions then this is a good book for you.

demonstrations.item_text:
The Mammy
Hardcover – Large Print, January 1, 2000

"Mammy" is what Irish children call their mothers and The Mammy is Agnes Browne--a widow struggling to raise seven children in a North Dublin neighborhood in the 1960s. Popular Irish comedian Brendan O'Carroll chronicles the comic misadventures of this large and lively family with raw humor and great affection. Forced to be mother, father, and referee to her battling clan, the ever-resourceful Agnes Browne occasionally finds a spare moment to trade gossip and quips with her best pal Marion Monks (alias "The Kaiser") and even finds herself pursued by the amorous Frenchman who runs the local pizza parlor. Like the novels of Roddy Doyle, The Mammy features pitch-perfect dialogue, lightning wit, and a host of colorful characters. Earthy and exuberant, the novel brilliantly captures the brash energy and cheerful irreverence of working-class Irish life.
demonstrations.review: Brendan O'Carroll is a fantastic storyteller.  Loved the book and would advise for people to read the series.  The book reminded me of sitting down with a friend who could keep us mesmerized with simple, home style stories.

demonstrations.item_text:
The Never-Bored Kid Book, Ages 7-8
Paperback – Teacher's Edition, June 1, 2006

While being engaged in fun activities, your children will be practicing important age-appropriate skills such as visual discrimination, sequencing, small muscle coordination, following directions, reading, and critical and creative thinking.
